For the past 5+ hours I've been running a Raspberry Pi Zero W on a solar panel and a 2000 mAh battery (which was charged using light only). So far so good.

Nice! What's the intended use for this Pi?

Embedded systems can run on SUPER low power if you drop the clock speed and use interrupts to bring it back. We're talking nanoamps for an ATTiny85.

At the moment it's just idling but it has a night vision camera installed and I'm thinking it would be fun to set up a all night webcam aimed at my pet Gerbils. But mainly I recently upgraded my solar charger to a 1 square foot panel and wanted to see how long it can power an actual computer.

Oh and I have several ATTiny85 chips and similar. I really love those little 8 pin ones with lots of ram (that's the 85, right). And arduino can be overkill. I you just want to control and LED or something small they're awesome

ATtiny85 is awesome! The little guy has 512 or 256 bytes of RAM, if I recall. 8K for onboard instructions, but I've still never felt cramped. Only thing that sucks is their lack of I2C by default, but that's not a big deal - you can install a library for it if you really need to.

As someone with next to no knowledge of network commands and higher level stuff, Arduino is perfect. I've often thought of a Pi for NAS or some other network device, but never actually pulled the trigger on that project.

I just think it's awesome how if you trim your power usage down, it's possible to make a pair of good lithium AAs last months or more of active use. No mucking around with solar or other power sources. We're truly living in the future, man.
